summary.title: MQTT broker from scratch: Refactoring & eventloop
summary.one_liner: Learn how a toy C MQTT broker was refactored to handle partial TCP reads/writes with a per-client state machine, a plain-or-TLS connection abstraction, and a portable epoll-style event loop.
takeaways: TCP is a stream protocol, so MQTT packets can arrive fragmented and must be read incrementally.
A per-client state machine (WAITING_HEADER, WAITING_LENGTH, WAITING_DATA, SENDING_DATA) lets non-blocking reads and writes resume after EAGAIN.
A connection struct with accept/send/recv/close callbacks lets the same code path serve plain and TLS clients.
A small ev abstraction hides the multiplexing backend (epoll now; select or kqueue could be plugged in) behind read/write callbacks.
summary.summary: The author revisits a toy MQTT broker written in C after six earlier parts and refactors it for structure and portability. The main fixes are handling TCP fragmentation with non-blocking reads and writes driven by a per-client state machine, and adding a connection abstraction so plain and TLS communication share one interface. The post also introduces a minimal event loop (ev) that wraps epoll behind a backend-neutral API, and swaps the hand-written hashtable for the uthash library. Code excerpts from the client struct, recv_packet, write_data, network.h and ev.h illustrate the design.
